reason: E1 shows that some Mg-containing lightweight HEAs are unstable against compound segregation and require specialized processing to freeze a metastable state, directly supporting the first premise. E2 demonstrates kinetic suppression of intermetallic phases by rapid cooling in a different HEA system, supporting the generalizability premise but not directly addressing Mg-containing alloys or the corrosion/oxidation consequences. The second premise (homogeneity improves corrosion/oxidation resistance) is not supported by the cited evidence, which contains no corrosion or oxidation data.
premises: Rapid quenching can kinetically freeze a metastable solid-solution state in Mg-containing lightweight HEAs, suppressing intermetallic formation.
A homogeneous solid-solution microstructure promotes continuous passivating oxide films and minimizes microgalvanic cells, enhancing corrosion and oxidation resistance.
Slow cooling or mild annealing allows partial transformation into intermetallic-containing microstructures.
The kinetic suppression of phases by rapid cooling is a generalizable mechanism applicable to Mg-containing lightweight HEAs.
